ideas.what: New '--patch forkblob' for the x138 base (a sibling of forkmid, same place: the very last graph edit, after linefit, after the insertion and after forkmid). For every 2-child fork whose added edge has safe_division == 1 and not div_inserted: read frame t+1 via the notebook's own read_test_frame (frames are usually already in repair_frame_cache from the DeepCenter veto). Blur only a local crop (gaussian sigma zyx 0.6/1.5/1.5 voxels). Compute valley = min of the interior 20-80% of the intensity profile on the segment c1->c2 divided by min(I(c1), I(c2)). If sister distance <= 5.0 um AND valley >= 0.95 (both daughters on ONE blob), drop the added edge the way forkmid does (the ILP-side edge if its edge_prob == 0.0, else the added edge). Nodes are never touched. FORKBLOB_ENABLE=0 gives a byte-identical output; the stage is wrapped in 'FORKBLOB FAILED' fail-soft; log 'FORKBLOB <clip>: vetoed k of n'. Thresholds are pre-registered NOW from GT statistics, with no lab tuning. Rides in K3 (K2 + forkmid + forkblob) as a separate knob.
ideas.why_now: This is new against the closed list, which has forkmid geometry, DeepCenter threshold, budget ladders, mirror daughter and 2nd daughter by edge features, but no image evidence at forks. Linajea+csc (Hirsch et al. MICCAI 2022) shows the division FPs are removed by cell-state (image) evidence, not by geometry: 'the inclusion of the classifier lowers [false divisions] drastically'. We cannot train a classifier (R9), but its cheapest training-free proxy discriminates strongly on our own data. I measured it today on local data. x138 forks (exp56 dummy CSV = x138 verbatim, 4 train clips): 15/62 = 24% have sisters <= 5 um on one blob at t+1, all with valley >= 0.95 (median 1.02). All 151 GT train divisions: only 3/151 = 2.0% look like that (GT sister median 10.6 um, valley median 0.63). That is a ~12x enrichment. The 15 flagged forks still have sisters only 5.3-8.0 um apart at t+2, against a GT first-daughter-frame median of 10.6 um (only 22/151 GT <= 7 um). So they look like duplicate detections kept alive by the divergence gate (>= 2.25 um) and by KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS, not like real forks placed one frame early. forkmid touches a different population: 2/62 forks (3.2%) with a far parent, while a one-blob fork has its parent near both sisters. The mechanism was diagnosed on the old base (memory: the ranker 'picks duplicate detections'), but no filter for it was ever built.
ideas.evidence: Prototype scripts and outputs are in the session scratchpad (forkvalley.py, forkvalley2.py, gtsister.py, forkvalley_exp56.csv, gtsister.csv). Inputs: _dl/biohub-exp56-x138-verbatim/submission.csv, biohub-cell-tracking-during-development/train/*.zarr|*.geff, tools/trainlab.official_eval. Fork labels on the 4 dummies: all 62 are 'ignored' by the official metric (0 TP / 0 FP; 3 GT div FN on 6bba_05db0fb1), so the dummies cannot show the sign. The exp60 lab (99 GT divisions) can. Control nearest-neighbour pairs of non-fork nodes: 3-5 um v>=0.95 67% (n=12), 5-7 um 39%, 7-9 um 22%. Safe-division code and gates: x138 cell 5, add_safe_divisions_postlink (parent<=9, sister<=14, mutual NN, divergence 2.25, DeepCenter>=0.25 at the candidate only, symmetry 0.6). Caps are not binding (35/6/5/16 added; browser_intel.md §6.0B). Literature: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11467 (csc in ILP, Table 2); ITEC https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.03.12.711203v1.full (merge 'two in this frame, one in neighbours' over-segmentation). Official division rules: tools/official/metrics.md l.51-128. A fork is FP only when it matches a GT node with outgoing edges or has local GT evidence.
ideas.expected_gain: Per event: removing one evaluable FP fork gives dJ ~ +J/S; losing one TP gives -1/S (S = div TP+FP+FN). Break-even is FP:TP ~ 1/J ~ 2.8 inside the vetoed cell. The GT base rate (2% of real divisions look one-blob) against 24% of forks predicts a ratio far above that, if the early-fork risk stays small. Public: central +0.001 (range -0.002..+0.003; P(<0) ~0.2). The division term is lumpy: one public fork event is ~0.001-0.004 of score. Private: +0.0005..+0.0015, lower variance (71% of clips). It targets the densest FP class of forks, so it is more likely than forkmid to be visible at the 0.001 step.
ideas.runtime_cost: About 15 forks/clip x one crop blur and one line sample. Frames are mostly cached, otherwise one blosc read of ~20-50 ms. That is < 1-2 s/clip, ~2-3 min over N~100, after the insertion, so it cannot push the 8.0 h DIVINS gate. Negligible against the ~4 h headroom.
ideas.test_gate: (0) Pre-registration (write into CONTEXT before any lab number is seen): thresholds s1 <= 5.0 um, v1 >= 0.95, sigma (0.6,1.5,1.5), safe-division forks only; no other values are tried. (1) Lab: add arm 'forkblob' (and 'forkmid45+forkblob') to tools/trainlab.py score, which already runs on the laptop with --train-dir, so the images are local. Run on the exp60 dumps (shard A pushed 17:15 UTC, B queued). Gate on SELECTION then CONFIRMATION halves, per embryo: vetoed forks with TP label <= 1 per 3 vetoed FP, and div_J(arm) >= div_J(control) on both halves; adj_edge unchanged by construction (nodes identical; any edge-J change must come from the dropped edges only). Kill if the lab shows >= 2 TP forks vetoed and FP:TP < 2.8, or if < 10% of the lab's control forks fall in the cell (dose too small). (2) Dummy gate on K3: nodes byte-equal to K2; forks removed only where the rule fires, and for the exp56-base forks the count equals this prototype's dose (15 of the 62 base forks, minus any already removed by forkmid); 'FORKBLOB FAILED' absent; FORKBLOB_ENABLE=0 build sha256 == K2 dummy. (3) LB: treated like C04 under R3 (nodes untouched: accept if public >= previous stack - 0.001 after the lab gate).
ideas.effort_hours: Patch + unit tests (copy of forkmid's harness): 2-2.5 h. Lab arm: 1 h. Scoring 56 clips on CPU: ~0.5-1 h (the blur is local crops only). K3 rebuild + dummy: 0.7 GPU-h on vitaliineibauer. Fits before the R8 cutoff (27 Sep 12:00) if K3 moves to ~26 Sep afternoon.
ideas.risk: (a) Real divisions forked one frame early on an elongated anaphase nucleus look identical at t+1. Only the lab labels can bound this; the t+2 distances argue against it. (b) Sparse 44b6 labels mean most lab evidence comes from 6bba (88 of 99 lab divisions). (c) Valley depends on intensity normalisation and blur; the rule is fixed from GT stats, not tuned. (d) It adds a fork-set change on top of forkmid in one slot, so if K3 < K2 - 0.001 both riders fall together; the lab arms separate their effects.

ideas.what: For every build after K2 (K3, K3b, K4, F1-final): raise BIOHUB_DIVINS_DEADLINE_S 28,800 -> 32,400 (9.0 h) and REPAIR_DEADLINE_S 34,200 -> 37,800 (10.5 h), now that the Kaggle limit is confirmed at 12 h (Code Requirements) and the hidden rerun covers public+private in one run. All new riders (forkmid, forkblob) go after the insertion, so they cannot delay its gate. Byte-identical whenever no timer fires. No new code: two --set values, and safetail's builder check must accept them (today it hard-requires 34200 unless --lab).
ideas.why_now: The binding runtime constraint in the current plan is not 12 h but K2's own insertion gate: forecast <= ~7.8 h against the 8.0 h DIVINS gate is a worst-case margin of only ~0.2 h (~7 s/clip at N~100; step0.md). Every rider that runs before the insertion, or a slower hidden machine, eats that margin and silently turns the insertion off on the alphabetically last clips. The 8.0 h value was chosen so that #35 and K2 would be comparable, back when the limit was thought to be ~9 h (FINAL_REPORT §a2). With 12 h confirmed, ~2 h of the ~4 h headroom can move into the gates while still leaving >= 1.5 h for the degraded fallback (seconds per clip) and the CSV write.
ideas.evidence: experiments/runtime_step0/step0.md (T(N) = 300 + N/2*318 + N*r; r = 56.6 s x138, 122.9 s exp57b; N <= 97-106; K2 <= ~7.8 h); CONTEXT.md 25 Sep 13:58 (12 h limit; errored submissions count toward the daily limit); FINAL_REPORT §e R5/R6 and the safetail build lines (REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200 enforced).
ideas.expected_gain: Tiny in expectation: P(runtime in 8.0-9.0 h) ~0.05-0.1 x insertion value on the skipped clips (<= +0.001 x fraction skipped) = ~+0.0001. Its value is removing a cliff for K3/K4 and F1-final. It also lets the rule 'any new rider must cost < 7 s/clip' be relaxed to '< ~40 s/clip'.

Add one lab-only dummy with DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=1 on the K3 build: 'DIVINS SKIPPED (deadline)' on every clip, CSV == the no-insertion twin. The builder test in tests/test_safetail.py must accept 37800. ideas.risk: The hidden machine could be much slower than the dummy estimate AND N near the upper bound: a 10.5 h deadline leaves ~1.5 h for fallback writing of the remaining clips (fast) before the 12 h hard stop. If the queue time inside the latency is unknown, keep 10.0 h instead of 10.5 h.

ideas.what: An alternative to K3b (the global DeepCenter threshold); lab-only unless strong. Keep x138's DeepCenter 0.25 veto, but re-admit a geometric safe-division candidate that DeepCenter rejected only when the image shows a division, all three required: (i) two blobs at t+1 (valley < 0.85) with sister distance 7-14 um (the GT core: median 10.6 um, valley median 0.51 at 9-12 um); (ii) daughter shrinkage: the half-max blob volume of each daughter at t+1..t+2 < 0.8 x the parent's at t-1 (zhincez: dividing nuclei shrink by ~27% at +3 frames, peak intensity holds); (iii) all existing geometric gates passed. It is a fork ADDER (R4), so only lab-validated, and at most an F2 candidate.
ideas.why_now: DeepCenter was trained only on the 71 44b6 clips and rejects 84/121, 149/155, 8/13 and 203/222 geometric candidates on the dummies (96% on the densest 6bba clip). A global threshold drop (K3b) re-admits duplicates together with real divisions. The forkblob measurement shows one-blob duplicates are ~24% of the admitted forks already, so a lower threshold probably raises that share further. Image evidence targets the real-division signature (two blobs, shrinking) rather than a centre-prior score. Linajea's cell-state classes (parent/daughter) are exactly this signal. Not in the closed list: mirror/lowdet daughters were about recovering nodes, and the 2nd daughter by edge features is a different signal.
ideas.evidence: browser_intel.md §6.0B (DeepCenter rejects); §6.1 item 2 (DeepCenter split = 71 44b6 train / 128 6bba val); CONTEXT.md l.210 (zhincez size profile; B20 diagnosis); scratchpad gtsister.csv (GT sister/valley per band); exp60 lab dumps hold the pre-safe-division graph and the DeepCenter score of every candidate (tools/trainlab.py docstring).
ideas.expected_gain: Public central +0.0005 (range -0.003..+0.003); P(lab gate) ~0.2. Adding forks has an asymmetric downside (FP forks cost on annotated parents).
ideas.runtime_cost: ~2-10 s/clip: 3 crops per candidate over DeepCenter-rejected geometric candidates, tens to ~200 per clip. It must sit inside add_safe_divisions_postlink, i.e. BEFORE the insertion, so it needs L2's gate retune first.
ideas.test_gate: Lab-only, CPU, laptop: replay from the presafe dump with the rescue arm. Pre-registered gate: rescued forks FP:TP <= 1:1 among evaluable forks on SELECTION, div_J up on both halves and both embryos, nodes identical. If it passes, then a K dummy (nodes == parent build) and, per R4, one LB probe only as an F2 candidate. Otherwise drop it. Never run it together with K3b's threshold change.
ideas.effort_hours: 3-4 h (half-max volume on local crops + arm) + scoring; patch only if the lab passes (+2 h).
ideas.risk: Low precision (non-division neighbour pairs at 7-9 um are two blobs in 58% of cases, so the shrink cue must carry the discrimination); few lab positives (99 divisions); a fork adder that fails R4 wastes a slot. It needs the R8 cutoff (27 Sep 12:00) for any kernel.

plan_critique: 1) Division riders: the one measurement I could add today changes the picture of fork FPs. Of x138's forks, 24% (15/62 on the dummies) are one-blob duplicates at t+1, against 2% of GT divisions. forkmid addresses only 3.2% (2/62). The exp60 fork audit (T9) should therefore record image features per fork: sister distance, valley at t+1/t+2 and blob volume. Also pre-register forkblob's thresholds in CONTEXT BEFORE the lab numbers arrive, like C04. 2) K3b (lower DeepCenter threshold) will most likely admit more duplicates. Evaluate it in the lab together with forkblob, or replace it by the image-evidence rescue (L3). Do not submit K3b without knowing the one-blob share of the extra forks. 3) Runtime: the plan still reasons with ~9 h numbers. With 12 h confirmed, the tight constraint is K2's own 8.0 h insertion gate (worst-case margin ~0.2 h = ~7 s/clip). Rule: every new rider runs after the insertion (forkmid and forkblob do). Move the gates (DIVINS 9.0 h, REPAIR 10.5 h) in K3+ (L2). 4) Literature cross-check: every large published division gain (linajea cell-state classifier in the ILP, OrganoidTracker 2.0 division net, DivNet-like pair models) needs a trained classifier. B20 showed the public DivNet as a ranker costs -0.014 locally. So nothing inference-only on the division side is worth more than ~+0.001-0.002. The same holds for linking: HOCT/Trackastra need masks + training, and OrganoidTracker's marginal-probability filtering is the closed edge-filter line on this metric. No new literature line justifies a slot beyond the image-evidence fork filters. 5) Keep the discipline: forkblob and forkmid both remove only forks (nodes untouched), so treat them as one K3 'fork-clean' build under R3 with per-arm lab gates. Do not add a second fork-set changer to the same slot.
